title: Diff digest: quick fixes, smoke tests, and next steps
content:
Context:
Small digest from reviewing PR #2783 (model routing batcher changes + KV cache tweak). Mostly smallish patches but a few spots that could bite in production if we don't add quick guards/tests. Written as my personal scratchpad; shareable with the team after cleanup.

High-level summary:
- Purpose: improve batcher latency tail and avoid unnecessary KV cache invalidations for single-token prefix updates.
- Scope: batcher scheduling logic (batch_window + early_full), KV cache eviction condition, metrics labels added, minor API param rename (timeout_ms -> req_timeout_ms).
- Risk: medium — behavioral change in scheduling + cache invalidation could cause subtle latency regressions or cache misses when under skewed request sizes.

Quick blockers / must-fix before merge (blocking if not addressed):
[ ] Add unit to ensure KV eviction only triggers when seq_len decreases by > threshold (currently fires on equal-length updates). Ticket: JIRA-4432 (added to linked_artifacts). Owner: Priya.
[ ] Fix timeout rename backward-compat check — library consumers may still pass "timeout_ms"; add compatibility shim and deprecation warning. Owner: Marcus.

Quick non-blocking but recommended fixes (low effort):
- Reduce log level for per-batch debug logs to debug (spam at info today).
- In batcher metrics, add a label "batch_origin" with values {api, internal, replay} — helps separate SLO analysis. (Zoe volunteered to add in follow-up).
- Inline comment: explain why early_full threshold is 0.85 — add reference to microbenchmark or link.

Tests to add (smoke + regression):
- Smoke: exercise batcher with skewed sequence length distribution (many short, few long) and assert mean latency stays within 2x baseline. Small harness: simulate 10k requests with 90% length<=8, 10% length>=512.
- Regression: KV cache must retain entries across single-token updates; add unit where update prefix length == old length -> expect cache hit.
- Integration: run a quick end-to-end with 2 GPUs local sim to validate no deadlocks when early_full triggers concurrently with eviction. Keep X seconds timeout to detect stalls.

Refactor ideas (not urgent, medium effort):
1) Split the batcher scheduler into two smaller collaborators: "windowing" and "decision". Right now both live in scheduler.go (~650 LOC) which is hard to test. Benefits: easier unit testing for decision logic and swap-in alternative schedulers later. Estimated 3-4d.
2) Extract an interface for KVCache with metrics hooks. Current implementation mixes eviction policy + metrics emission; if we expose an interface we can A/B different eviction heuristics (LRU vs size-based) without touching serving path.
3) Consider moving the "compat shims" for API param renames behind a feature flag for 2 releases; avoid long-lived complexity.

Rollout plan (canary -> global):
- Canary 1 (internal): enable on internal tier only, 1% traffic, monitor token/req latencies and cache-hit ratio for 48h.
- Canary 2 (customer-facing): 10% traffic, with automatic rollback if 95th-percentile latency increases > 15% or cache-hit ratio drops > 10% relative to baseline.
- Global: after 72h stable at 10% and 48h stable at 1% with satisfied SLOs.

Monitoring and dashboards to review post-merge (metric names):
- batcher.request_latency_ms.p95 (per model variant)
- kvcache.hit_ratio (filter by model, shard)
- serving.errors.rate (increase would indicate regressions)
- cpu.gpu_utilization (watch for unexpected spike due to smaller batches)
- logs: "kv-evict" occurrences per minute

Follow-ups / longer-term wishlist (ticket/owners):
- JIRA-4501: Batcher microbench harness and long-tail simulation (Owner: Oliver).
- JIRA-4502: KV cache interface + LRU prototype (Owner: Priya).
- JIRA-4503: Scheduler refactor spike (Owner: Marcus).

Notes to self / reviewer heuristics (how I skimmed this diff):
- Grep for "evict" and "invalidate" to find cache touch points.
- Check callsites for req_timeout_ms rename; search across repo for "timeout_ms" and add compatibility tests.
- Evaluate whether added metrics have dimensions that can cardinality-explode (avoid user_id-level labels).

Random thoughts / brain dump (unstructured):
- If we see cache-hit drop after rollout, likely culprit: eviction condition being too eager on small deltas — easier to debug if we had per-shard eviction histograms (counts by decision reason).
- Maybe we should log a small sample of requests that triggered eviction with hashed context id so we can correlate with trace ids. But be careful with PII.
- The scheduler change seems safe but needs stress-testing under heavy multi-tenant scenarios; can we run with a synthetic mix in staging next week?

Next immediate actions (today / 48h):
1) Open small PR that adds the compatibility shim for timeout rename + a unit test. (Marcus)
2) Add the single-unit test for KV eviction condition (Priya).
3) Add a short smoke-run script to ci/smoke/batch-smoke.sh and run in my laptop env; results to be uploaded to the PR as artifacts. (Oliver)

If you're reviewing: focus on "what changed for cache behavior" and "how we will detect regressions in canary". If anything looks risky but necessary, call it out and propose a mitigation (feature flag, reduced rollout).

-- Oliver
